key_insight: An ion-pumped SrFeO3−δ thin film can reversibly switch between brownmillerite and perovskite phases, enabling continuous analog control of optical transmittance and color.
engineering_relevance: This offers a low-power, nonvolatile route to tunable electrochromic and photonic devices that is more compatible with oxide electronics and silicon photonics than many conventional materials.
method: Drive oxygen-ion redox in SrFeO3−δ thin films
Induce reversible structural phase transitions between brownmillerite and perovskite
Add an optically passive Al2O3 interference layer to enhance optical modulation
evidence_signal: The abstract reports pronounced changes in electronic structure and optical constants, with continuous and reversible modulation of transmittance and color across the phase transition.
watch_item: Practical deployment will depend on maintaining fast, repeatable oxygen-ion pumping while preserving long-term structural stability and device durability.
paper_title: Structure-driven analog optical control in ion-pumped SrFeO$_{3-δ}$ thin-film devices
